chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Wahb, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Lu'lu'i, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from a man, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning:
A man performs ghusl on Friday or otherwise; does it suffice for him in place of wudu (ablution)? So Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: And what wudu (ablution) is purer than ghusl?

So the proper approach regarding these reports is that we carry them to mean that when these, or some of them, are combined with ghusl of janabah, then the obligation of wudu (ablution) falls away; but when these ghusls, or some of them, are separate from ghusl of janabah, then wudu (ablution) is obligatory before them, according to what has preceded, and what follows further clarifies that.

key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: the reports, meaning the transmitted hadith narrations
key_terms.الْجُمُعَةَ: Friday, referring here to the Friday ghusl
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing required before certain acts of worship
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ghusl of janabah, the ritual bath for major ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: Does Friday ghusl or another ghusl suffice instead of wudu (ablution) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report addresses whether other ritual baths, such as the Friday ghusl, suffice in place of wudu (ablution). The concluding legal clarification states that the dropping of wudu applies when such ghusls are combined with ghusl of janabah, whereas if they are performed independently of ghusl of janabah, wudu remains obligatory.
